spec: Spell out the English ordinal word for integers 1 through 12 ('first' through 'twelfth'); for any other integer, return its plain number followed by 'th' (e.g. '13th', '21th').

Join a list of strings into a natural-language list: an empty list gives an empty string, a single item is returned as-is, two items are joined with ' and ', and three or more items are comma-separated with 'and' before the final item (Oxford comma style).

Given a template string with placeholders of the form {key} and a dictionary mapping every such key to a value, replace each placeholder with the string form of its corresponding value and return the result. Assume every placeholder in the template has a matching key in the dictionary.

Given a template string with placeholders of the form {key}, a dictionary of known values, and a default string, replace every placeholder with its value from the dictionary if present, or with the default string if the key is missing from the dictionary.

Given a template string with {field} placeholders and a list of record dictionaries, render the template once per record by substituting each record's field values, and return the list of rendered strings in the same order as the records. Assume every placeholder has a matching key in every record.

Given a template string containing one or more '___' blank markers and a list of words, replace each blank with the next word from the list, in order, and return the filled string. Assume the number of blanks matches the number of words.
visible_tests: assert fill_blanks('The ___ jumped over the ___.', ['cat', 'fence']) == 'The cat jumped over the fence.'
assert fill_blanks('___ is here', ['Sam']) == 'Sam is here'

spec: Return a greeting string combining a time of day and a name, formatted exactly as 'Good {time_of_day}, {name}!'.
Join a list of string fields into a single CSV line separated by commas, wrapping any field that contains a comma or a double quote in double quotes and doubling any internal double quote characters.
Capitalize only the first character of a string, leaving the rest of the string unchanged. An empty string is returned unchanged.
Given a paragraph made of sentences separated by '. ' (period then space), capitalize the first letter of each sentence and rejoin them with '. '.
visible_tests: assert capitalize_sentences('hello world. this is a test.') == 'Hello world. This is a test.'
assert capitalize_sentences('one sentence only') == 'One sentence only'
assert capitalize_sentences('first. second. third.') == 'First. Second. Third.'

spec: Swap the case of every alphabetic character in a string (uppercase becomes lowercase and vice versa), leaving non-alphabetic characters unchanged.

Mask the local part of an email address (the part before the '@'): keep the first and last character visible and replace every character in between with '*', keeping the domain part unchanged. If the local part is only one character, leave it as-is; if it is two characters, mask the second with '*'.
Given a list of words, prefix each one with '#' and join them with single spaces into one string.
Count the number of whitespace-separated words in a string and format it as '{n} word' when there is exactly one word, or '{n} words' otherwise (including zero).
Given a list of item strings, format them as a bulleted list where each item is prefixed with '- ' and items are joined by newlines.
Given a list of item strings, format them as a numbered list where each item is prefixed with its 1-based index followed by '. ', and items are joined by newlines.
Run-length encode a string: replace every maximal run of the same consecutive character with that character followed by the run's length as a decimal number. An empty string returns an empty string.
Expand a run-length encoded string (pairs of a single letter followed by a decimal count) back into the repeated characters, concatenated in order.
Convert a 24-hour hour (0-23) and minute (0-59) into a 12-hour clock string 'H:MM AM' or 'H:MM PM', where midnight is displayed as 12 AM and noon is displayed as 12 PM.
Convert a 12-hour hour (1-12), minute (0-59), and 'AM' or 'PM' period into a 24-hour clock string 'HH:MM', where 12 AM becomes hour 00 and 12 PM stays as hour 12.
Convert a snake_case string (words separated by underscores) into a human-readable title by capitalizing each word and joining them with single spaces.

Normalize all line endings in a text to plain '
', converting every '
' pair and every standalone '' into a single '
'.
Given an email address whose local part (before the '@') consists of dot-separated name components, return the uppercase initials formed from the first letter of each component, in order.
Format a dictionary as a single string of comma-and-space-separated 'key=value' pairs, ordered by sorted key.
Format a numeric range as 'start-end', unless start and end are equal, in which case return just the single number as a string.
Abbreviate a full month name to its first three letters, with only the first letter capitalized (e.g. 'January' becomes 'Jan').
Given a three-letter month abbreviation (in any letter case), return the full month name. If the abbreviation is not one of the twelve standard ones, return it unchanged.
Format a home score and an away score as a string 'home - away' with single spaces around the hyphen.

Given a positive numerator and positive denominator forming an improper or proper fraction, convert it into a mixed number string: if the numerator is exactly divisible, return just the whole number; if the whole part is zero, return just the reduced fractional part 'a/b'; otherwise return 'whole a/b' with the remainder fraction reduced to lowest terms.
Join a list of lowercase words into a single camelCase string: the first word stays lowercase and every subsequent word is capitalized, with no separators. An empty list returns an empty string.
Join a list of lowercase words into a single PascalCase string by capitalizing each word and concatenating them with no separators. An empty list returns an empty string.
Join a list of words into a single snake_case string by lowercasing every word and joining them with underscores. An empty list returns an empty string.

Given a list of string cells and a list of column widths of the same length, left-justify each cell with spaces to its column width and join the columns with ' | '. If a cell is already at least as long as its width, leave it unpadded (do not truncate).

Given a list of string cells and a list of column widths of the same length, right-justify each cell with spaces to its column width and join the columns with ' | '. If a cell is already at least as long as its width, leave it unpadded (do not truncate).

Given cells, matching column widths, and a list of one-letter alignment codes ('l' for left, 'r' for right, 'c' for center), pad each cell to its width using the requested alignment, then join the columns with a single space. Alignment codes are given per column and lists are always the same length.
Given a list of cells and matching column widths, left-justify each cell to its width and format the row as a grid line: a leading '| ', the padded cells joined by ' | ', and a trailing ' |'.
Given cells, matching widths, and a separator string, left-justify each cell to its width with spaces and join the padded cells together using the given separator string.

Given cells and matching widths, force each cell to exactly its column width: if the cell is longer than the width, cut it down to the first width characters; if it is shorter, left-justify it with trailing spaces. Join the resulting fixed-width columns with a single space.

Given a list of (key, value) pairs and a fixed key column width, render one line per pair: the key left-justified with spaces to key_width immediately followed by the string form of the value. Join the lines with newline characters. An empty list of pairs produces an empty string.

Split text on whitespace into words, then greedily pack the words into lines separated by single spaces so that no line exceeds width characters. A single word longer than width is placed alone on its own line without being split. Return the list of lines; an empty or all-whitespace text returns an empty list.
visible_tests: assert wrap_greedy('the quick brown fox', 10) == ['the quick', 'brown fox']
assert wrap_greedy('a b c d', 3) == ['a b', 'c d']
